Trigger: When finalizing an image-plane answer such as “transverse plane or coronal plane,” especially for a chest radiograph whose rationale mentions an AP/PA frontal view.

Observable verification action: Check the actual image or raw imaging observation for the plane-defining feature: a frontal chest projection showing both lungs, the heart, and the spine together supports the coronal plane, whereas an axial cross-sectional slice supports the transverse plane. Select the plane only when that observed feature matches it; if no current-image observation is present, retrieve or rerun orientation verification rather than relying on the reference answer. In this case the rationale describes a frontal chest X-ray and the terminal text matches the reference “Coronal Plane,” but the transcript contains no raw image/tool observation, so the correct grade alone does not prove the procedure. Since the options map was empty, there is no letter mapping to check; if options were displayed, the supported plane text should be mapped back to its displayed choice and the letter and text should agree.
